QUOTE: "Library sources that include `common.h` see the real field names." Also: "Without the opt-out, `ctx->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(state)` becomes `ctx->private_state`, so the real name `state` no longer exists. Plain `ctx->state` then fails to compile."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer shows the two branches of the macro and says that code defining the opt-out sees plain member names, while code that doesn't define it sees the `private_` renamed ones.
